verses.text: Then Zophar, the Naamathite, answered,
“Shouldn’t the multitude of words be answered? Should a man full of talk be justified?
lines: “Shouldn’t the multitude of words be answered?
Should a man full of talk be justified?

verses.text: Should your boastings make men hold their peace? When you mock, will no man make you ashamed?
lines: Should your boastings make men hold their peace?
When you mock, will no man make you ashamed?

verses.text: For you say, ‘My doctrine is pure. I am clean in your eyes.’
lines: For you say, ‘My doctrine is pure.
I am clean in your eyes.’

verses.text: But oh that God would speak, and open his lips against you,
lines: But oh that God would speak,
and open his lips against you,

verses.text: that he would show you the secrets of wisdom! For true wisdom has two sides. Know therefore that God exacts of you less than your iniquity deserves.
lines: that he would show you the secrets of wisdom!
For true wisdom has two sides.
Know therefore that God exacts of you less than your iniquity deserves.

verses.text: “Can you fathom the mystery of God? Or can you probe the limits of the Almighty?
lines: “Can you fathom the mystery of God?
Or can you probe the limits of the Almighty?

verses.text: They are high as heaven. What can you do? They are deeper than Sheol. What can you know?
lines: They are high as heaven. What can you do?
They are deeper than Sheol. What can you know?

verses.text: Its measure is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.
lines: Its measure is longer than the earth,
and broader than the sea.

verses.text: If he passes by, or confines, or convenes a court, then who can oppose him?
lines: If he passes by, or confines,
or convenes a court, then who can oppose him?

verses.text: For he knows false men. He sees iniquity also, even though he doesn’t consider it.
lines: For he knows false men.
He sees iniquity also, even though he doesn’t consider it.

verses.text: An empty-headed man becomes wise when a man is born as a wild donkey’s colt.
lines: An empty-headed man becomes wise
when a man is born as a wild donkey’s colt.

verses.text: “If you set your heart aright, stretch out your hands toward him.
lines: “If you set your heart aright,
stretch out your hands toward him.

verses.text: If iniquity is in your hand, put it far away. Don’t let unrighteousness dwell in your tents.
lines: If iniquity is in your hand, put it far away.
Don’t let unrighteousness dwell in your tents.

verses.text: Surely then you will lift up your face without spot; Yes, you will be steadfast, and will not fear:
lines: Surely then you will lift up your face without spot;
Yes, you will be steadfast, and will not fear:

verses.text: for you will forget your misery. You will remember it like waters that have passed away.
lines: for you will forget your misery.
You will remember it like waters that have passed away.

verses.text: Life will be clearer than the noonday. Though there is darkness, it will be as the morning.
lines: Life will be clearer than the noonday.
Though there is darkness, it will be as the morning.

verses.text: You will be secure, because there is hope. Yes, you will search, and will take your rest in safety.
lines: You will be secure, because there is hope.
Yes, you will search, and will take your rest in safety.

verses.text: Also you will lie down, and no one will make you afraid. Yes, many will court your favor.
lines: Also you will lie down, and no one will make you afraid.
Yes, many will court your favor.

verses.text: But the eyes of the wicked will fail. They will have no way to flee. Their hope will be the giving up of the spirit.”
lines: But the eyes of the wicked will fail.
They will have no way to flee.
Their hope will be the giving up of the spirit.”
